title: Sable and the Summit
premise: Edmund Dunmore has spent seven years flying medicine and mail into the interior, hiding from a manslaughter charge he never believed was his to carry. When a geological survey expedition upriver goes silent, the company that once ruined him offers him a contract to fly in supplies—and Edmund discovers the expedition's leader is the man whose testimony convicted him. Forced down by engine trouble beyond the range, Edmund must cross the mountains on foot with the expedition's sole survivor, a cartographer named Sable Voss, who knows what the survey really found: a gold seam the company intends to seize by burning out the valley's homesteaders. Racing the dry season's last weeks and the first snows, Edmund chooses at last between staying invisible and becoming the witness the valley needs, testifying to justice outside any courtroom and finding his name worth carrying again.
about_author: August Lockridge is the pen name of a former bush pilot turned writer who spent six years flying supply runs across the northern interior before trading the yoke for the keyboard. Lockridge writes adventure fiction about people who live where maps run thin.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A routine medicine run over the interior establishes Edmund's exile, his careful routines, and the radio silence he prefers. He measures life in miles flown, not years lived. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness, faintly cracked when a passenger mentions the survey expedition upriver.

chapters.title: The Silent Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The expedition stops answering scheduled check-ins; the company, Meridian Consolidated, offers Edmund a lucrative contract to fly supplies—signed by an executive he recognizes from his trial. He refuses, then can't stop thinking about it. Beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: A Name He Buried
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, flashback woven through present. We learn of the crash seven years ago, the death pinned on him, and the testimony of surveyor Alden Crane that sealed it. Meridian doubles its offer. Beat: old shame resurfacing as anger.

chapters.title: Contract of Convenience
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Needing parts for his own failing plane, Edmund signs on—telling himself it's just cargo. He loads drums, chain, and crates he isn't allowed to inspect. Beat: self-deception tightening into complicity.

chapters.title: The Last Good Field
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. His final fuel stop is a homesteader strip where families speak nervously of surveyors staking claims. An old woman asks him to carry a letter out if he can. Beat: warmth and foreboding—the valley is real to him now.

chapters.title: Down in the White
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Engine failure above the range forces a crash landing on a high plateau short of the expedition camp. Injured but alive, Edmund salvages the radio—it's dead—and spots smoke days away. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: POV Sable Voss. The expedition's mapmaker, half-starved after walking out of a camp that 'went wrong,' finds Edmund's wreck. She trusts no one, carries a satchel she won't explain, and knows the way through the pass. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She reveals the truth: a rich gold seam beneath the homestead valley, and orders to falsify boundaries so Meridian can claim it. The camp split; Crane's men destroyed the evidence cache. Her satchel holds the only true maps. Beat: moral stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Crane's Voice on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the abandoned forward camp they find Crane alive, holding court with armed men and the missing supplies. Crane recognizes Edmund instantly—and offers him redemption in exchange for taking Sable's satchel back. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Debt
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, night scene. Crane privately admits the testimony was bought, offering to recant if Edmund helps contain Sable. Edmund nearly says yes. Beat: the lowest point—power offered as forgiveness.

chapters.title: Theft in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Sable. She steals the satchel back and wakes Edmund to flee before dawn; he goes with her, choosing her truth over Crane's bargain. They're spotted crossing the river flats. Beat: commitment—the point of no return.

chapters.title: River of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Pursued downstream, they find the homestead strip burned—Meridian's 'accidental' fire already lit. The old woman's letter, still in Edmund's jacket, names the families now scattered. Beat: grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Pass Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The climb begins: scree, cold nights, Edmund's untreated wound turning septic. Sable navigates by stars and memory while Edmund fights fever. Beat: endurance and growing mutual trust.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, delirious interlude. Hallucinations braid the old crash with the new one; Sable keeps him alive with willow bark and blunt honesty, telling him his name doesn't have to be a sentence. Beat: identity confronted.

chapters.title: The Summit
chapters.summary: POV Sable. They crest the range as the first snows fall behind them—a day later and the pass closes. From the summit they see the valley, the smoke, and a company plane shuttling men south. Beat: awe and urgency.

chapters.title: Descent into the Valley
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. They descend to find the homesteaders regrouping at a mission station, leaderless and afraid. Edmund reveals who he is—the pilot who flew for the company—and asks them to listen anyway. Beat: vulnerability as leadership.

chapters.title: Sable's Maps, Edmund's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Together they lay out the true boundary maps and Edmund's account of Crane's confession. The homesteaders plan to intercept the company's claim filing at the district office, three days' travel. Beat: justice organized outside the law.

chapters.title: Crane Comes Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Crane's party arrives at the station demanding the satchel; a tense standoff ends when two of Crane's own men defect after seeing the burned homesteads. Beat: power fracturing under truth.

chapters.title: The Race to the District Office
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A breakneck journey by raft and borrowed truck to file the maps and affidavits before Meridian's claim registers. Crane pursues; Edmund's wound reopens. Beat: rising action at full sprint.

chapters.title: Climax: The Weight of a Signature
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the office, Crane arrives with lawyers and lies; Edmund publicly takes back his silence, naming his own crime and Crane's bought testimony alike. The clerk accepts Sable's maps and the homesteaders' counter-claim. Beat: catharsis—truth spoken at cost.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Crane is arrested for arson and fraud; Edmund surrenders himself on the old manslaughter charge, trusting the new evidence. Waiting in custody, he feels lighter than he has in seven years. Beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: First Flight of Spring
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, epilogue. Cleared after trial, Edmund returns to the interior—not invisible now, but known. He flies the mail route past the rebuilt homesteads, Sable beside him mapping the honest lines. Beat: resolution—identity reclaimed, home found in motion.
